First I create some simulated data to work on, and the I save all my results as a data frame.  
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
sim <- Sim_Fit(
  GroupNames = c("KinPair1", "KinPair2"),
  GroupSizes = c(2000, 2000),
  nIter = 10,
  SSeed = 2,
  GroupRel = c(.5, 0.25),
  GroupR_c = c(1, 1),
  mu = c(15, 15), 
  ace1 = c(.3, .2, .5),
  ace2 = c(.3, .2, .5),
  ifComb = FALSE,
  lbound = FALSE,
  saveRaw = TRUE)

df_list <- map(sim, ~ as.data.frame(.x$data))
list2env(df_list, envir = .GlobalEnv)
```

The next step is to make it plausible for drug initation data - that means some people need to have NAs to represent non-use. I also have to make this into a loop or use the map function to scale it up to handle all the iterations. 

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results='hide'}
for (i in 1:length(df_list)) {
  
  df_list[[i]] <- df_list[[i]] %>%

 mutate(y1 = case_when(
    R == .5 ~ ifelse(runif(n()) < 0.20, NA, y1), 
     R == .25 ~ ifelse(runif(n()) < 0.10, NA, y1)))  %>%
    
  mutate(y2 = case_when(
    is.na(y1) ~ NA, 
    TRUE ~ y2
  )) %>%
  mutate(Ord_1 = case_when(
    y1 <= 14 ~ 1,
  y1 <= 15 ~ 2,      #does this make sense or do people end up with multiple numbers by doing it this way  -- it seems like its working OK just eyeballing my iterations ord var. 
  y1 <= 16 ~ 3,
  y1 >= 17 ~ 4,
  is.na(y1) ~ 4,
  ),
  Ord_2 = case_when(
    y2 <= 14 ~ 1,
  y2 <= 15 ~ 2,
  y2 <= 16 ~ 3,
  y2 >= 17 ~ 4,
 is.na(y2) ~ 4,
  )) %>%
  mutate(RCoef = R)
}

list2env(df_list, envir = .GlobalEnv)
```

I got mad trying to plot a path diagram with the openMx functions (they are totally useless and don't work with my mxobjects, which is ironic). So I asked Gemini how it would do this, given an openMx ACE output. For your entertainment, this is what it gave me. 

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(DiagrammeR)

# Create the diagram using the values calculated above
DiagrammeR::grViz(paste0("
digraph ACE_Model {
  graph [layout = neato, overlap = FALSE, outputorder = edgesfirst]
  
  # Latent Variables
  node [shape = circle, fixedsize = true, width = 0.8]
  A [label = 'A']; C [label = 'C']; E [label = 'E']
  
  # Observed Variable
  node [shape = box, fixedsize = true, width = 1.2]
  Trait [label = 'Observed\nTrait']
  
  # Paths and Labels
  A -> Trait [label = '", round(a2, 2), "']
  C -> Trait [label = '", round(c2, 2), "']
  E -> Trait [label = '", round(e2, 2), "']
}
"))
```

```{r}
stand3 <- function(data) {
  # 1. Access the parameters table from the summary
  params <- data$sum$parameters
  
  # 2. Pull the 'Estimate' value where the 'name' matches your labels
  # We use [1] at the end just to ensure we get a single numeric value
  A <- params$Estimate[params$name == "VA11"]
  C <- params$Estimate[params$name == "VC11"]
  E <- params$Estimate[params$name == "VE11"]
  
  # 3. Calculation
  V  <- (A + C + E)
  a2 <- A / V
  c2 <- C / V
  e2 <- E / V
  
  # 4. Return as a clean row
  estACE <- rbind(cbind(a2,c2,e2))
  return(estACE)
}

# Run the apply
estimates_list2 <- lapply(results, stand3)

# Combine into one big table
correct_results <- do.call(rbind, estimates_list2)
correct_df <- as.data.frame(correct_results)
kable(correct_df)
```
